later_uses_not_recorded.name: 1979-1980 Plymouth Volare Duster package
later_uses_not_recorded.finding: Only Wikipedia-derived pages and one newspaper column mention it (one excerpt gives 5,586 built in 1980). Fewer than three reputable sources were found, so no engine rows are recorded.

later_uses_not_recorded.name: 1982/1985-1987 Plymouth Turismo Duster (Omni/Horizon-based coupe)
later_uses_not_recorded.finding: Wikipedia (Dodge Omni and L-body Charger articles), Motor Authority ('Guilty pleasure: Plymouth Turismo Duster', https://www.motorauthority.com/news/1058710_guilty-pleasure-plymouth-turismo-duster) and Curbside Classic name a Turismo Duster package, so three sources confirm the name. Wikipedia's Omni article dates the 2.2 HO 'Turismo Duster' to 1982, while its Charger article says the name was revived in 1985. A 96 hp 2.2L appears in search excerpts only. It is a different car on a different platform, and its engines were not verified here.

later_uses_not_recorded.name: 1992-1994 Plymouth Sundance Duster
later_uses_not_recorded.finding: Not in the brief. Wikipedia, Autoblog ('Junkyard Gem: 1993 Plymouth Sundance Duster') and Consumer Guide name it as a V6 package (3.0L Mitsubishi 6G72, about 141 hp per excerpts). Different car; engines not verified.

later_uses_not_recorded.name: Plymouth Trail Duster (1974-1981)
later_uses_not_recorded.finding: A truck/SUV unrelated to the A-body Duster. Excluded.

notes: NHRA lists exactly the engines recorded for each year, except the 1975 California 360.
Factory brochures (Plymouth, counted as ONE source) confirm the engine lineup for every year; HP is printed only in the 1970 and 1971 sheets.
No EPA data (pre-1984; epa_duster.json is empty).
